mapNode.detail: Four of us have bought a tile cutter and none of us has used it twice.
mapNode.label: A tool library for the street

mapNode.detail: Six were still running after two years; five had folded inside one.
mapNode.label: Looked at eleven street tool libraries

mapNode.detail: Shared custody was the strongest predictor of a library folding.
mapNode.label: Every one that lasted had a single named keyholder

mapNode.detail: Every organiser who tried a subscription described it as the point it stopped feeling like a favour.
mapNode.label: None of them charged money, and none of them wanted to

mapNode.detail: Every write-up stops at the launch. What breaks, and who stops turning up, is unrecorded.
mapNode.label: Nobody tracks what happens after the first winter

mapNode.detail: Take the three things every surviving library had and nothing else.
mapNode.label: One keyholder, one shelf, no money

mapNode.detail: The thing that keeps it alive is the thing that can end it.
mapNode.label: One keyholder is also one person who can move away

message.content: A tool library for the street - nobody needs to own a tile cutter, and four of us have bought one.
Before proposing anything, I went and looked at what already exists.

description: A round that is entirely research, on the real route: the row wears its own tinted ground, a hairline enclosure and the eyebrow WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so what has already been looked up reads as its own territory before any card in it is read. The round above it is unbanded, so the contrast is in one frame. The map's other research scenario is the boundary case — exactly half its round is research, which is not a majority, so it correctly gets no band.
